Q: Why do integration tests remove IDbContextOptionsConfiguration<TContext> instead of the DbContext itself A:

Your line of thinking is likely "substitute the DbContext" when their example is "remove the configured injected Options for the DbContext and set up for In Memory". For unit testing we typically want to avoid interacting with a "real" DbContext for performance reasons. Unit tests are intended to be run repeatedly through iterative development, while integration tests are run regularly prior to integrating/committing changes.

For integration testing though, I wouldn't recommend using an in-memory database as query behaviour between the real RDBMS will differ from in-memory. Integration tests should closely reproduce a production environment with a known data state. This ensures the behaviour matches production, and can help test & highlight issues with query performance. Mocked DbContext interactions and even in-memory database queries can often differ in behaviour from a real RDBMS call through the EF provider, leading to potential issues going unnoticed, or false flags raised because of differences with in-memory queries & operations.

Q: "django.db.utils.NutSupportedError: extension 'postgis' not available" error being thrown despite having postgis installed in Python virtualenv A:

It is neither Django nor Python issue. Especially venv has nothing to do with it. Using apt in venv or not installs packages globally in your OS. This issue is solely between your Postgres and Postigs system-wide installations.

I did reproduce your setup using your Postgres and Postgis installation commands (in reverse order and with required sudo apt update after repo update) in Ubuntu 24.04.03. In my setup Postgis extension can be created with CREATE EXTENSION postgis;.

What might be wrong in your setup

You can check whether packages are installed or not, using apt list --installed. In my working setup I get:

$ apt list --installed postgis postgresql-18
postgis/noble-pgdg,now 3.6.1+dfsg-1.pgdg24.04+1 amd64 [installed]
postgresql-18/noble-pgdg,now 18.1-1.pgdg24.04+2 amd64 [installed]

As all apt installations are system-wide, If you are running more than one Postgres servers in one OS you might end up connecting to wrong one.
For example if you install packages in following order

$ sudo apt install postgresql-17
$ sudo apt install postgresql-18
$ sudo apt install postgis

and then not configure anything, you will probably get a conflict. Reasoning from my tests it looks like the first Postgres you installed is ran by default. But apt doesn't know whichever you are running, so Postgis will be installed for Postgresql 18, the latest one. Default systemd postgres service will still serve Postgres 17.
You can check if you are on correct Postgres version by running

SELECT version();

while connected to db, or

$ pg_lsclusters

in shell.
If you serve wrong one, which I find highly probable, to create a new one you can use

$ pg_createcluster 18 pg18

Note that this command will list new (configurable) port that you will have to use in your app configuration.

Note: I am aware this answer contains assumptions that might be not correct. After OP gives more insights on their setup I will edit.

Q: Trac EmailVerification by AccountManager not working after upgrade A:

After some digging, I have figured out the root cause. Posting here so that other people can save their time for something better...

This was caused by an slightly insidious configuration issue...

  • the installation hat quite some tweaks regarding the log-in over time
  • with one of the recent versions, seemingly a new component was added, the AccountNotificationFormatter
  • we had detailed enabled/disabled settings in the trac.ini and this component was not enabled.
  • on new user email verification, the EmailDistributor uses an implementation of INotificationFormatter -- which in fact is assumed to be provided by the AccountNotificationFormatter. This whole exchange just serves the purpose to indicate that the notification shall be sent in format text/plain, but missing this configuration, the EmailDistributor just bails out with the quoted message.

Solution: ensure acct_mgr.notification.AccountNotificationFormatter = enabled in (trac.ini) -- mybe better set acct_mgr.notification.* = enabled

Related code...

  • the EmailDistributor is implemented in <trac>/notification/mail.py

    • transport ≡ email
    • event.realm ≡ account
       def distribute(self, transport, recipients, event): 
          if transport != 'email': 
              return 
          formats = {} 
          for f in self.formatters: 
              for style, realm in f.get_supported_styles(transport): 
                  if realm == event.realm: 
                      formats[style] = f 
          if not formats: 
              self.log.error("%s No formats found for %s %s", 
                             self.__class__.__name__, transport, event.realm) 
              return
  • the INotificationFormatter is supplied by <acct_mgr>/notification.py
class AccountNotificationFormatter(Component):

    implements(IEmailDecorator, INotificationFormatter)

    realm = 'account'

    # INotificationFormatter methods

    def get_supported_styles(self, transport):
        yield 'text/plain', self.realm

Q: Neural network backpropagation with RELU A:

Yes - with ReLU, if a neuron’s pre-activation a <= 0, its local derivative is 0, so the gradient through that neuron is blocked for that example. This does not kill gradient descent for the whole network; it only affects that unit on that data point. Other neurons (and other samples) can still propagate gradients normally.

Below is a step-by-step backpropagation for your architecture:

input -> hidden linear -> ReLU -> output linear -> softmax

Forward pass (single example)

Let x be the input vector.

  1. Hidden pre-activation:
a = W1 * x + b1
  1. ReLU activation:
h = max(0, a)
  1. Output logits:
z = W2 * h + b2
  1. Softmax:
p_k = exp(z_k) / sum_j exp(z_j)
  1. Cross-entropy loss (one-hot label y):
L = - sum_k y_k * log(p_k)

Backward pass (single example)

Step A: softmax + cross-entropy gradient

A useful simplification:

dL/dz = p - y

Call this:

delta2 = p - y

Step B: gradients for output layer

dL/dW2 = delta2 * h^T
dL/db2 = delta2

Step C: backprop into hidden activations

dL/dh = W2^T * delta2

Step D: backprop through ReLU

ReLU derivative is elementwise:

ReLU'(a_i) = 0  if a_i <= 0
             1  if a_i > 0

So:

dL/da = (dL/dh) * indicator(a > 0)

This is the key point:

  • If a_i <= 0, then dL/da_i = 0 → that neuron does not update for this example.

  • If a_i > 0, the gradient passes through unchanged.

Call this:

delta1 = dL/da

Step E: gradients for first layer

dL/dW1 = delta1 * x^T
dL/db1 = delta1

Does ReLU “kill” learning when a <= 0?

  • It kills the gradient through that neuron for that example.

  • Other neurons that are active (a > 0) still learn.

  • The output layer always receives gradients.

  • Over a batch, a neuron can be inactive for some samples and active for others.

A real problem only appears if a neuron is always inactive (a <= 0 for all inputs), in which case it becomes a dead ReLU and never updates.

Common mitigations:

  • Proper initialization (He initialization)

  • Reasonable learning rates

  • Using Leaky ReLU or PReLU if dead neurons are frequent

For a more intuitive explanation with visuals, you can also check:
https://lossmatters.com/blog/relu

Q: Numerical estimate of derivative for stochastic process A:

.... due to the inherent noise present

OK, so first you should find out how much noise is present. Reduce the range of the random value ( e.g. np.random.normal(0.95, 1) ). Vary the range to see the effect of the noise. I suspect that your noise is so large at (0,1) that your particles are taking random walks and there is no such thing as "an accurate estimate of the slope"

Q: Having references in the collision-detection struct (etc.) to Vec items that represents collision objects (etc.) A:

Your items is a shareable mutable container. You can use Cell.

Cell<T> has getter, setter and replacer so you can do mostly anything with it. It is more for types that implement Copy. Otherwise, RefCell can be used. RefCell replaces compiler-time checks with runtime checks, allowing to relax compilation rules at the cost it may panic at runtime if your algorithm is not sound.
